result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.generate_random_paths()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Sample random paths, as Panther similarity does. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.generate_random_paths()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Sample random paths, as Panther similarity does. title: >- [Graph.generate_random_paths()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Sample random paths, as Panther similarity does. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Sample random paths, as Panther similarity does. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L29651-L29732){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.generate_random_paths( sample_size, path_length=5, weighted=None, seed=None, source=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Generate random paths](/assets/graphs/generate-random-paths.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three copies of a six-node cycle, one per sampled path of length 4 (five nodes, seed 2). Each path's edges and nodes are in its own color, accent, teal and violet, and filled badges give each node's positions along the path, 0 for the start. The first path, 6, 1, 6, 1, 2, steps back and forth before moving on; the third, 5, 6, 5, 6, 5, never leaves one edge." width="100%"} Each path starts at `source` or, if none is given, at a uniformly random node with out-edges of positive weight, and takes `path_length` random steps, each to a neighbor (an out-neighbor in a directed graph) chosen with probability proportional to the edge weight. Nodes may repeat, since a step can go back. These are the paths `panther_similarity()` samples, and they suit other walk-based estimates too, such as how often nodes co-occur or how far walks travel. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sample_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The number of paths. [path_length]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The number of steps in each path, so each path holds `path_length + 1` nodes. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag; edges without a weight count as `1.0`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : If given (as an ID or label), every path starts at this node. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The paths, each as a list of node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source` doesn't exist, a weight is negative, no node has out-edges (when there is no `source`), or a path reaches a node with no out-edges (an isolated `source`, or a sink in a directed graph). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A step from node $u$ moves to $v$ with probability $A_{uv} / \sum_x A_{ux}$, where $A$ is the weighted adjacency matrix (parallel edges add up, as in NetworkX's `to_numpy_array`). Skipping isolated nodes (and sinks) as random starts follows the fix in NetworkX pull request #8578; NetworkX releases without it may start a walk at an isolated node and fail. This matches NetworkX's `generate_random_paths`, which returns a generator and can also fill an `index_map` of node to path indices; here the paths come back as a list, from which such an index is a short loop. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#41996982 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(6) graph.generate_random_paths(3, path_length=4, seed=2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [[6, 1, 6, 1, 2], [5, 6, 5, 4, 3], [5, 6, 5, 6, 5]] ``` ::: :::
